tool.name: miRTrace Trace
tool.description: clade-specific miRNA profile for contamination detection
tool.command:
mirtrace trace --output-dir . --force #if $adapter: --adapter '$adapter' #end if --protocol '$protocol' #if $write_fasta: --write-fasta #if $uncollapse_fasta: --uncollapse-fasta #end if #end if #if str($title).strip(): --title '$title' #end if #if str($comment).strip(): --comment '$comment' #end if --num-threads \${GALAXY_SLOTS:-4} #echo ' '.join(map(str, $sample))# &&
## Move output files cp mirtrace-report.html '$report_html' && cp mirtrace-results.json '$results_json' && cp mirtrace-stats-contamination_basic.tsv '$stats_contamination_basic' && cp mirtrace-stats-contamination_detailed.tsv '$stats_contamination_detailed' &&
## Collect FASTA outputs if requested #if $write_fasta: tar -czf '$fasta_qc_passed' -C output qc_passed_reads.all.collapsed 2>/dev/null || true #end if
tool.help:
**miRTrace Trace** detects clade-specific miRNA contamination in small RNA sequencing data.
.. class:: infomark
miRTrace is a tool for quality control and tracing of small RNA sequencing data.
-----
**Trace Mode**
In Trace mode, miRTrace produces a clade-specific miRNA profile report. This is useful to identify potential cross-species or cross-sample contamination.
**Output files:**
- ``mirtrace-report.html`` – interactive HTML report with clade-specific miRNA profile - ``mirtrace-results.json`` – all results in JSON format - ``mirtrace-stats-contamination_basic.tsv`` – clade-specific miRNA counts (Matrix 6) - ``mirtrace-stats-contamination_detailed.tsv`` – detailed clade-specific miRNA counts (Matrix 7)
-----
**Use case example**
If you suspect that your samples may be contaminated with RNAs from another species (e.g. rodent RNA in a human sample), Trace mode can quantify clade-specific miRNA fractions to confirm or rule out contamination.
-----
**References**
Kang W et al. (2018) miRTrace reveals the organismal origins of microRNA sequencing data. *Genome Biology*, 19, 213. https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-018-1588-9
